title: Carolyn Goerig v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained. The SJC held that Pacific Northwest Presbytery erred in denying Carolyn Goerig's December 23, 2001 complaint. Because Faith Presbyterian Church (Tacoma) Session did not follow BCO 38-4 regarding her membership, the Presbytery should have remanded the case to the Session. No separate issue-level dispositions appear.
first_summary: Carolyn Goerig complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery wrongly denied her complaint against Faith Presbyterian Church (Tacoma) Session, which had banned her from attending and treated her membership as subject to retroactive erasure. The SJC sustained the complaint, reasoning that she remained a member under BCO 46-3 and that the Session failed to follow BCO 38-4. The Presbytery should have remanded the case to the Session.
summary: A church member challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery's denial of her complaint that Faith Presbyterian Church (Tacoma) Session had banned her from worship and sought to erase her membership retroactively under BCO 38-4. The SJC sustained the complaint. Because she never joined Covenant PCA, BCO 46-3 left her membership under Faith's Session; the Session's proposed retroactive erasure did not comply with BCO 38-4's pastoral-oversight steps. The Presbytery therefore erred and should have remanded the matter to the Session. No separate merits relief beyond that remand directive appears.
